liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **So Many Roads (take 1)** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Notes list So Many Roads run as chord changes five times, then intro four times, then four more passes; Reviewer calls So Many Roads one of Jerry's last great songs, with strong Hunter lyrics [1][3][4]
- **Chuck Berry & Weir on Ketamine** (2 reviews): Bobby's comic Chuck Berry bit hints at NRPS and an altered state of mind; Reviewer especially enjoys Weir's story connecting NRPS and ketamine [3][6]
- **Cowboy song** (1 other source): Notes name the cowboy numbers as Got a Horse and Along the Navajo Trail [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **Garcia teaches So Many Roads chords to band**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **So Many Roads (take 3)**: cut on the recording [14]
- **Chuck Berry & Weir on Ketamine**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Cowboy song**: back after 1575 archived shows (7988 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]
- **Topsy Part 1 (Cozy Cole)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Phil teaches Wave to the Wind chords to band**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **It's a Man's Man's Man's World (Vince singing lead)**: back after 1539 archived shows (7826 days); rare: 8 archived performances [14]
- **Wave to the Wind**: earliest performance in the archive; cut on the recording [14]

## The recordings

- **gd92-02-21.smr-rehersal.8189.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 13 songs; 47 min; rated 4.56/5 by 18 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the recording very nice sounding, giving an intimate look at a relaxed band session; Reviewer says the sound is decent [3][5]

## Around the show

- Phil, Jerry and Bobby trade plenty of banter during the relaxed rehearsal session [2]
- Bob worries about learning his So Many Roads part before the next night's Alameda show [4]
- Bobby tries to sound like a musical genius at the end of each take [4]
- The session shows the band working through the creation of new songs, with some banter [5]
- Phil and Jerry trade tongue-in-cheek banter throughout, with Garcia's quick wit prominent [10]
- Reviewer recalls first hearing So Many Roads in Oakland [12]
- Reviewer's lost tape had this material plus a try or two at Corinna with strong Garcia playing [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd92-02-21.smr-rehersal.8189.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Seeded to abgd by Doo Dah Man; an MD5 was generated from the original SHN files for the etree database [1]
